goals: Mechanistic: characterize runoff generation (surface runoff vs subsurface drainage; rain vs snowmelt timing) across the Naches elevation and soil gradient
Validation: compare simulated runoff to USGS stream gauge discharge (latent, see feasibility)

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM resolves the vertical water balance and snowpack that generate runoff locally; NLDAS forcing makes elevation act through precip/temperature across this 1625 m relief, and SSURGO gives the soil lever.

answerable: Elevation control on runoff generation via NLDAS elevation-resolved precip/temperature and simulated snow (rain-snow transition, melt timing)
Soil-texture control on surface-runoff vs drainage partitioning
Column-local runoff terms (QOVER surface runoff, QDRAI drainage, total QRUNOFF)

not_answerable.aspect: Validation of simulated runoff against USGS stream gauge discharge
not_answerable.why: Single-column, no lateral transport/routing: independent 1-D columns produce no integrated basin streamflow, so gauge discharge cannot be reproduced co-located
not_answerable.needs: runoff routing / column aggregation to basin outlet

not_answerable.why: Slow states cold-start at default ~8.8 m water table; recharge reads ~0 while storage fills
not_answerable.needs: spin-up years or Fan-2013 WTD-informed warm start

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (elevation bands x dominant soil classes), transect-biased along valley->ridge
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 3 elevation bands span the rain->snow gradient that dominates runoff timing; within each band the 2-3 dominant SSURGO textures (expander-selected, not all 9 combos) isolate the infiltration-partitioning control. ~8 columns span the strata with light replication in the rain-snow transition band where runoff mechanism switches — the smallest set that resolves both drivers.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate columns in the mid-elevation rain-snow transition (800-1400 m) where melt-driven vs rain-driven runoff generation and soil control are strongest; anchor one column low (valley) and one high (snow-dominated) as gradient endpoints. Honor the user's valley->ridge transect intent.
sampling_strategy.replication: One extra column in the transition band to sample a second dominant soil there, since that band is where the runoff mechanism transitions.

sampling_plan.reason: Rain-dominated basin floor; establishes low-elevation surface-runoff/drainage baseline across coarse vs fine soil.
Core of the runoff question: samples where melt vs rain timing switches, replicated across dominant soils to isolate infiltration control.
Snowmelt-driven runoff generation endpoint; tests high-elevation SWE and melt partitioning.

validation_design.comparison: aggregated — NOT possible without routing; a qualitative comparison of column-summed runoff seasonality vs gauge hydrograph shape is the best available, and is only indicative, not co-located
validation_design.metric: seasonal-timing correlation (qualitative) — quantitative bias/NSE blocked until routing exists
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — gauge count/locations not provided in brief

validation_design.observation_source: SNOTEL (if any in-domain — not listed in brief)
validation_design.comparison: analog / not confirmed — flagged as gap; would provide the only direct check on the snowmelt driver

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: NLDAS-2 forcing (elevation-resolved), native SSURGO soil, WTD-informed warm start

requires_capabilities.capability: runoff routing / column aggregation to basin outlet
requires_capabilities.why: convert independent column runoff into integrated streamflow
requires_capabilities.blocks: co-located USGS gauge validation — the only in-domain observation

requires_capabilities.capability: spin-up years or Fan-2013 WTD-informed warm start
requires_capabilities.why: slow subsurface states cold-start at default water table

requires_capabilities.capability: DEM/elevation sampling + SSURGO soil raster expander
requires_capabilities.why: turn elevation/soil strata rules into concrete in-domain columns
constrain columns to the true watershed, not just bbox
validate the snowmelt driver central to runoff timing

assumptions: User point (46.62, -119.90) is OUTSIDE the domain bbox (lon -119.90 vs eastern limit -120.5) — treated as an error and excluded; the other two points inform the valley->ridge transect intent but are not used as literal coordinates.
Domain is CONUS -> NLDAS-2 forcing applies and gives elevation-resolved precip/temperature.
Dominant SSURGO textures per elevation band are selected downstream by the expander; the 3 listed classes are placeholders.
Runoff generation studied here is column-local partitioning, not basin-integrated discharge.
open_questions: How many USGS gauges are in-domain and where (outlet vs tributary)? Needed to scope any future routing-based validation.
Should the out-of-domain user point be corrected to an intended in-domain location, or dropped?
Are SNOTEL stations available in-domain to validate the snow driver?
